facts.text: NASA-STD-7009B and ASME V&V 40 retain physical testing where model risk is high, meaning high influence on the decision combined with severe consequences.
facts.quote: physical testing is kept where model risk is high (high influence on the decision combined with severe consequences)

facts.text: NASA-STD-7009B and ASME V&V 40 retain physical testing where validation evidence is weakest.
facts.quote: physical testing is kept where model risk is high (high influence on the decision combined with severe consequences) and where validation evidence is weakest.

facts.text: In NRC EMDAP, PIRT ranks phenomena; highly ranked phenomena need integral and separate-effects test data, while low-ranked phenomena receive reduced emphasis.
facts.quote: the PIRT ranks phenomena; highly ranked phenomena need integral and separate-effects test data, low-ranked ones get reduced emphasis.

facts.text: FAA AC 20-146A requires a baseline seat to be supported by dynamic testing.
facts.quote: **FAA AC 20-146A:** a baseline seat must be supported by dynamic testing.

facts.text: Under FAA AC 20-146A, once a seat model has shown acceptable agreement, eligible modifications within the defined family may be substantiated by simulation instead of another dynamic-test series.
facts.quote: Once the model has shown acceptable agreement, eligible modifications within the defined family may be substantiated by simulation instead of another dynamic-test series.

facts.text: Under FAA AC 20-146A, seat changes that alter major load-transfer paths, failure mechanisms, materials or seat-to-track interactions require new physical evidence.
facts.quote: Changes that alter major load-transfer paths, failure mechanisms, materials or seat-to-track interactions require new physical evidence.

facts.text: In EU 2022/1426 and NATM, physical tests both validate the toolchain and confirm the system; this is on-road evidence.
facts.quote: **EU 2022/1426 and NATM:** physical tests both validate the toolchain and confirm the system

facts.text: In EU 2022/1426 and NATM, virtual testing covers the operational design domain inside the validated envelope; this is on-road evidence.
facts.quote: virtual testing covers the operational design domain inside the validated envelope.

facts.text: The adopted on-road UN R152 approach retains physical confirmatory tests, with their number agreed with the authority.
facts.quote: **UN R152 (on-road):** the adopted approach keeps physical confirmatory tests, their number agreed with the authority.

facts.text: A vendor interprets the on-road UN R152 proposal as requiring a minimum of 30% physical tests, with at least one physical test per scenario variant.
facts.quote: A vendor reads the proposal as a minimum of 30% physical tests with at least one per scenario variant

facts.text: The UTAC CERAM working document AEBS-16-03 carries the figure “+ 30% Physical tests” for on-road virtual testing.
facts.quote: the UTAC CERAM working document AEBS-16-03 carries the same "+ 30% Physical tests" figure.

facts.text: An earlier UTAC technical-service presentation, informal document AEBS-12-07, “Validation Method: Virtual Testing,” stated that of “10 tests repeated each scenario,” 10% “can be taken away.”
facts.quote: An earlier UTAC proposal (informal document AEBS-12-07, "Validation Method: Virtual Testing"; technical-service presentation) stated that of "10 tests repeated each scenario", 10% "can be taken away"

facts.text: The earlier UTAC proposal AEBS-12-07, “Validation Method: Virtual Testing,” stated that virtual validation can be applied in a validity domain; this is on-road evidence.
facts.quote: "virtual validation can be applied in a validity domain"

facts.text: In rail practice, a simulation model is physically validated through stationary and on-track measurements.
facts.quote: **Rail:** the model is physically validated through stationary and on-track measurements

facts.text: After physical validation in rail practice, simulation may extend the assessed range of conditions, support modified-vehicle approval or make comparisons against an approved reference configuration.
facts.quote: simulation may then extend the assessed range of conditions, support modified-vehicle approval or make comparisons against an approved reference configuration.

facts.text: The synthesis of the NASA-STD-7009B, ASME V&V 40, NRC EMDAP, FAA AC 20-146A, EU 2022/1426, NATM, UN R152 and rail frameworks recommends splitting physical and virtual testing according to information value and extrapolation risk, not a percentage of the historical physical test matrix.
facts.quote: Across these, the split follows **information value and extrapolation risk**, not a percentage of the historical physical matrix.

facts.text: The framework synthesis identifies physical tests as the strongest candidates to retain when they establish a new phenomenon, validate the ends of the intended domain, expose coupled failure mechanisms, verify conditions with the smallest safety margin, test new sensor placement or physics, validate weather and contamination models, or investigate simulation discrepancies with earlier physical tests.
facts.quote: Physical tests are the strongest candidates to keep when they establish a new phenomenon, validate the ends of the intended domain, expose coupled failure mechanisms, verify conditions where the safety margin is smallest, test new sensor placement or physics, validate weather and contamination models

facts.text: The framework synthesis identifies simulation as strongest for replacing or expanding tests when the case is interpolation within a physically anchored domain, a parameter sweep around a validated configuration, repeated scenario variations exercising the same validated physics, or a closely related product variant whose differences can be bounded.
facts.quote: interpolation within a physically anchored domain, a parameter sweep around a validated configuration, repeated scenario variations that exercise the same validated physics, or a closely related product variant whose differences can be bounded.
